label: What's on
rationale: The timetable: a class, meeting or exam you have (all ga aru), then plans shifting: work coming up, something postponed.
mixUps: jugyou, kaigi and shiken all take ga aru, never motsu; shigoto ga hairu and enki ni naru say what happened to the plan, with no 'I' or 'they' doing it.

targets.trap: 'Have class' tempts jugyou o motsu, which only fits a teacher's teaching load. A class you go to just exists: jugyou ga aru.
targets.use: How students explain their day or turn down plans: ashita ichigen kara jugyou aru (I've got class from first period). Casual speech drops ga; jugyou nai means a free day or period.
targets.notes: In class right now is jugyou-chuu; skipping it is jugyou o saboru.

example.romaji: ashita asa kara jugyou aru n da.
example.ja: 明日朝から授業あるんだ。
example.english: I've got class first thing tomorrow.

examplePolite.romaji: ashita wa asa kara jugyou ga aru n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 明日は朝から授業があるんです。
examplePolite.english: I've got class first thing tomorrow.

targets.trap: 'Have a meeting' tempts kaigi o motsu, which only works as stiff 'hold a meeting' (the everyday 'hold' is kaigi o hiraku). A meeting on your calendar just exists: kaigi ga aru. Attending is kaigi ni deru; kaigi o deru is leaving the room.
targets.use: Said when explaining your schedule or why you can't talk: kore kara kaigi aru kara. Casual speech drops ga, and smaller team or client meetings are uchiawase, with the same verb.
targets.notes: Someone in one right now is kaigi-chuu: ima kaigi-chuu desu.

example.romaji: gomen, kore kara kaigi aru n da.
example.ja: ごめん、これから会議あるんだ。
example.english: Sorry, I've got a meeting now.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, kore kara kaigi ga aru n desu.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、これから会議があるんです。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, I've got a meeting now.

targets.trap: 'Have an exam' tempts shiken o motsu. An exam on your calendar exists: shiken ga aru. Sitting it is shiken o ukeru.
targets.use: Said when explaining plans or turning things down: raishuu shiken aru kara muri. Casual speech drops ga, and for school tests students say tesuto more than shiken.
targets.notes: Wishing someone luck before it: shiken ganbatte!

example.ja: 来週試験あるから、無理。
example.english: I've got an exam next week, so I can't.

examplePolite.romaji: raishuu shiken ga aru node, chotto muri desu.
examplePolite.ja: 来週試験があるので、ちょっと無理です。
examplePolite.english: I've got an exam next week, so I'm afraid I can't.

targets.verbSense: go in, enter; get put into something
targets.use: The standard reason for cancelling: kyuu ni shigoto haitchatta (work came up suddenly). Mostly in the past, or as haitteru (I've got work booked); ga is usually dropped.
targets.notes: Same frame as yotei ga hairu (see there for why not okiru). Freelancers and shops also use it for work coming in: atarashii shigoto ga haitta, yoyaku ga haitta.

example.ja: ごめん、急に仕事入っちゃった。
example.english: Sorry, something came up at work.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, kyuu ni shigoto ga haitchaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、急に仕事が入っちゃいました。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, something came up at work.

targets.trap: English 'was postponed' tempts the passive enki sareta, which sounds like an official notice. In conversation the event becomes postponed: enki ni natta, like chuushi ni naru (called off).
targets.use: Said when an event moves because of rain, illness or schedules: shiai, ame de enki ni natta. Mostly in the past (natta, natchatta), and the ni stays.
targets.notes: Moving it yourself is enki suru, or casually zurasu: raishuu ni zurasou.

example.romaji: ame de shiai enki ni natta.
example.ja: 雨で試合延期になった。
example.english: The game got postponed because of rain.

examplePolite.romaji: ame de shiai ga enki ni narimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 雨で試合が延期になりました。
examplePolite.english: The game was postponed because of rain.

reviewPool.english: go out for fun; go visit
speak to, call out to; ask along
play games (video games, cards and the like)
not feel well, be under the weather (the safe phrase at work)
be in good shape, going well
feel sick (queasy or faint); feel put off
